clinician.final_diagnosis: tertiary HPT had finally developed with persistent hypercalcemia, elevated serum PTH and an increase of the set-point calcium-PTH
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 70-year-old man with a history of renal failure on hemodialysis and secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) presented with symptoms of hypercalcemia. He was found to be in hypercalcemic crisis with an albumin-corrected calcium of 3.96 mmol/l (E001). His history included a PTH rise to 197.3 pmol/l with a normal calcium level of 2.06 mmol/l, indicating a shift in the calcium-PTH set-point. Initial parathyroid ultrasound was unremarkable (E002), but a Tc-99m dual-phases parathyroid scan detected a hyperfunctioning parathyroid gland (E006). Following surgical excision, histopathological examination revealed a 2 cm well-encapsulated mass (E007). Post-operatively, both calcium and PTH levels dropped stably and normalized (2.12 mmol/l and 21.41 pmol/l, respectively, within 10 days) and remained stable for 3 months (E008), confirming the diagnosis of tertiary HPT.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with hypercalcemic crisis, with serum albumin corrected calcium of 3.96 mmol/l and elevated ALP of 160 u/l.
Patient had a history of secondary hyperparathyroidism with PTH rising to 197.3 pmol/l with normal calcium (2.06 mmol/l), indicating an increase in the set-point calcium-PTH.
A Tc-99m dual-phases parathyroid scan detected a hyperfunctioning parathyroid gland.
Surgical excision was performed, and histopathological examination revealed a 2 cm well-encapsulated mass.
Post-surgery, calcium and PTH levels dropped stably and normalized, remaining stable for at least 3 months.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Patient's history of renal failure and secondary hyperparathyroidism makes primary HPT less likely as the initial cause, though tertiary HPT represents autonomous function similar to primary.
The presence of persistent hypercalcemia (3.96 mmol/l) and autonomous parathyroid function (hyperfunctioning gland on scan, normalization post-surgery) indicates progression beyond typical SHPT.
